title: Microsoft signs 'iron-clad' student privacy deal with teachers unions after NYC AI ban

title: Instead of managing billions, Warren Buffett’s son Howard Buffett chose farming
content: Choosing a path less traveled, Howard Buffett, the son of Warren Buffett, dedicated his life to farming and conservation rather than finance. He skillfully managed farms in Nebraska and Illinois, prioritizing soil health. Warren Buffett supported his passion by purchasing a Nebraska farm for his son. As he transitions to the role of non-executive chairman at Berkshire Hathaway, Howard aims to safeguard the company’s culture following his father's legacy.

title: Israel released 28 wild donkeys in desert; 44 years later, they created an oasis
content: In an effort to rejuvenate the parched landscape of Israel's Ramon Crater, wild donkeys were brought back into the ecosystem. These resilient animals played a crucial role by creating waterholes, which became essential for desert wildlife. Additionally, their droppings helped spread acacia seeds, promoting the growth of trees. Their natural movements resulted in water-retaining depressions, significantly transforming the area's ecology into a thriving environment that has caught global attention.

title: 3-minute intense exercise may beat 90-minute cycling, study finds

Comparatively, a prolonged session of moderate cycling for ninety minutes triggers only slight changes. This evidence suggests that while both short and long exercise sessions contribute uniquely to fitness and health, the effects of intense exercises promote rapid bodily upgrades.

title: 44 injured, 18-year-old critically hurt after train derails in northern France
content:
Transport Minister Philippe Tabarot said around 140 firefighters and emergency personnel were deployed to the scene

At least 44 people were injured, including one seriously, after a passenger train derailed in northern France on Friday evening, officials said. The train, carrying around 180 passengers, was travelling between Rouen and Caen when it went off the tracks near Cléon in Normandy, shortly before 20:00 local time. An 18-year-old woman was critically injured and airlifted to Rouen University Hospital, while 43 others reportedly suffered minor injuries. Transport Minister Philippe Tabarot said around 140 firefighters and emergency personnel were deployed to the scene. Uninjured passengers were taken to Cléon Town Hall. The cause of the derailment was not immediately known. SNCF reported significant disruption to rail services in the area and said replacement buses would be provided.
